analyses.claim: In the modeled SMG clitic reading, genitive and acc12 programs compete for the same locally unfixed address. Their incompatible requirements block the cluster; a third-person accusative has a fixed-node strategy.
analyses.limits: This card does not generalize the SMG restriction to Pontic or to strong-pronoun readings. An accepted prefix may retain an unfixed node. The supplied sentence has no independent corpus judgment in the workbench.

analyses.title: DS–TTR and TTR-DS: semantic content versus representing parsing in TTR

sources.version: Published 22-page 2025 article; fingerprint in the paper record.

sources.locator: §2 for DS–TTR/event semantics and §3 for DyLan.
§§2–3 for record updates and dialogue context.

analyses.claim: Earlier DS–TTR uses TTR content in DS processing. Cooper and Larsson explicitly call their recasting TTR-DS: DS tree descriptions, parse states and action rules are represented in TTR. The latter is an additional architectural proposal, not an interchangeable name for a record-semantic backend.
analyses.limits: CL25 recasts parts of DS and concentrates on classical e/t contents. §4.8 leaves further semantic integrations open; §5 describes a detailed implemented grammar as future work. Selected sections were inspected, not every formal rule. No new parser implementation or parity result is claimed by this card.

implementations.scope: The app’s Python executor and native Classical semantics have not been recast as CL25 TTR action rules.
The existing dependent-type compiler is distinct from the CL25 recasting.
The app has record-semantic types and DS tree/action execution; this does not implement the proposed TTR encoding of parsing itself.

analyses.next_action: Review §§3–4 rule by rule; specify a separate experimental TTR-DS parse-state/action prototype and its tests before any integration into the workbench.

sources.version: 396-page thesis PDF identified in the paper record.

analyses.claim: The transition from Koine to the Medieval varieties and from Medieval to the modern varieties is explained by routinisation (Pickering and Garrod 2004) and parsing/hearer asymmetries: an encoded clitic system emerges from a freer, pragmatically regulated one (author's account, abstract level).
